thread:
deploy-bot: INCIDENT detected: canary failure for rollout 'release-2026-03-canary' — 4/5 canary hosts returning 502 from inference-proxy. Severity: P2. @eng-oncall paging.

cora (oncall): seeing it. thanks deploy-bot. @mike can you grab logs for the canary group? is this a kernel/quant crash or routing? :eyes:

mike (eng-sre): hitting it now. quick note: errors spike only for models served on gpu-pool-eu (canary). other pools normal. requests timing out while waiting for kv-cache spinup, then 502s from proxy.

mike (eng-sre): pastes logs:
```
2026-03-15T12:01:22Z inference-proxy: upstream->model-worker: timeout waiting for kv_cache.init [model_id: gptx-3-open]
2026-03-15T12:01:22Z model-worker: failed to allocate quantized buffers, errno=12 (out of memory)
2026-03-15T12:01:23Z proxy: returning 502 to client
```

cora (oncall): looks like memory blow for this quantized build. was this canary using new quantization kernel? @lee

lee (platform): yes, canary was rolled with qkernel-v2, meant to reduce memory. suspicion: regression in per-batch allocation logic. rolling back kernel quickly is possible but we have feature-flag gates for rollout. two mitigation options:
- toggle feature flag off for canary (fast, no full rollback)
- kill the canary and route traffic to stable (rollback)

cora (oncall): we should minimize customer impact. do flag toggle first. @alex please prep customer comms if regression grows.

alex (support): on it. collecting recent incidents from EU customers. initial contact if >5% error rate for >10m. current rate ~3.2% of canary traffic, affects only EU region — no data loss reported. will draft note after we stabilize.

mike (eng-sre): running command to flip flag:
```
./ffctl set rollout.qkernel-v2 eu-canary false --reason "oncall: OOM regression causing 502s"
```

deploy-bot: Feature flag update accepted: rollout.qkernel-v2 (eu-canary) -> false. Propagation in progress (3/3 services).

mike (eng-sre): seeing immediate drop in 502s on canary proxy metrics. error rate down from 3.2% -> 0.6% in 90s. KV init errors stop appearing. Good sign.

cora (oncall): awesome. keep observing for 15m. @lee can we open a postmortem ticket and assign to runtime team? looks like qkernel-v2 has an allocation regression.

lee (platform): creating tracker: JIRA INF-8472. Assigning to @runtime-eng. I'll attach heap dumps and allocation traces.

julia (product): quick customer note suggestion: "We detected degraded responses for a small subset of EU traffic during a canary rollout; we've disabled the new kernel and traffic is healthy. No customer data was affected." I can sign off on wording.

alex (support): draft ready, DMing legal for the checklist, will send to affected customer list if we hold steady for 30m.

mike (eng-sre): marking the on-call runbook step completed: toggled flag, metrics recovered, creating debugging snapshot. Next: compare allocation profiles between qkernel-v1 and v2.

cora (oncall): handing off to @lee (day oncall) for follow-up (covers root cause & rollback plan) — Handoff at 12:15 UTC. Status: mitigated, feature flag disabled, customer impact limited to ~3% canary traffic briefly. No rollback executed.

lee (platform): taking it. I'll coordinate with runtime to prepare a safe rollback image if needed. We'll keep the canary disabled until we have a fix.

mike (eng-sre): note for postmortem: the canary gating should have caught allocation regression — we need a synthetic that stresses kv-cache warm paths for quant kernels.

cora (oncall): tagging incident as MONITORED. Please update INF-8472 with timeline and attach the command outputs and graphs. I'll close the page once legal & support confirm customer comms sent.

deploy-bot: INCIDENT update: status changed -> mitigated. responders: cora, mike, lee, alex. Link to alert: https://alerts.internal/1995123456

alex (support): legal cleared, comms out to 14 affected accounts at 12:42 UTC. no escalations yet.

lee (platform): scheduling postmortem meeting for 2026-03-16 15:00 UTC. attendees: runtime, platform, oncall, product.

cora (oncall): paging cleared for this thread. leaving notes: flip FF, observe 15m, create INF ticket, support comms OK. Great work everyone. :thumbsup:

mike (eng-sre): small follow-up after handoff: recommend a short-lived canary with qkernel-v2 on non-prod to reproduce reliably.

lee (platform): ack. creating non-prod repro job.

cora (oncall): last check: metrics stable for 20m, closing thread. If reoccur, re-pager to eng-oncall.
